name: Ebbeh (Cassava and Seafood Soup)
author: Yewande Komolafe
description: A deeply satisfying soup, with a rich medley of textures, ebbeh is meant to nourish — every spoonful a delicate, nuanced harmony of savory, sour and spicy. Sometimes called ebeh or yebeh, the soup is served year-round across the Atlantic coast of The Gambia, Sierra Leone and Senegal. Pieces of peeled starchy tubers are simmered in a broth enriched with red palm oil and spicy Scotch bonnets until they dissolve and thicken the soup. Traditional versions feature kong paing, a smoked catfish, soft-shell crab and a mix of small and large shrimp. This adaptation honors the original flavors but features substitutions like frozen peeled cassava chunks (though fresh peeled cassava can also be used). And if you cannot find kong, smoked whitefish is an adequate substitute, as is more lump crab meat. Chopped fresh cilantro and lime wedges complete this dish.

ingredients.raw: 1 (24-ounce) bag frozen cassava chunks, thawed, or 1 large fresh cassava
6 cups water, plus more as needed
¼ cup red palm oil  (see Tip)
2 Scotch bonnet chiles, halved, seeds in or out (depending on heat preference)
ingredients.preparation: halved, seeds in or out (depending on heat preference)

ingredients.raw: 1 teaspoon kosher salt (such as Diamond Crystal), plus more as needed
1 ½ pounds kong (smoked catfish) or smoked whitefish, picked of skin and bones to yield 2 cups flaked meat (see Tip)
ingredients.preparation: picked of skin and bones to yield 2 cups flaked meat (see Tip)

ingredients.raw: ½ cup tamarind paste or 2 tablespoons tamarind concentrate
ingredients.item: tamarind paste or 2 tablespoons tamarind concentrate

ingredients.raw: ½ bunch fresh cilantro leaves and stems (about 1 cup), chopped, divided
ingredients.item: fresh cilantro leaves and stems (about 1 cup)

ingredients.raw: 2 tablespoons fresh lime juice (from 2 limes), plus 1 lime cut into wedges
1 pound large shrimp, peeled and deveined

steps.text: Fill a medium bowl with tap water. If using frozen chunks, simply cut each piece in half and remove the fibrous, golden-hued thread. If using fresh cassava, trim off the ends with a sharp knife and slice cassava into 2-inch-thick rounds. Make a slit through the skin just deep enough for the knife to touch the white flesh. Peel off skin and discard. Halve each round, and remove the thread. Slice the cassava into 1-inch chunks and place in water as you go to keep them from turning brown.

Transfer the cassava to a large pot, along with 6 cups water, the red palm oil, Scotch bonnets and 1 teaspoon salt. Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat. Reduce heat to medium and cook, stirring frequently, until cassava just begins to soften (a knife should barely go through), about 12 minutes. Continue to cook until cassava is translucent and the liquid begins to thicken with slow, simmering bubbles rising, about 15 minutes more. (The chunks should break apart easily.) Crush cassava pieces against the side of the pot to thicken the sauce into a porridge-like consistency.
Stir in smoked fish, tamarind, half the cilantro and lime juice. Stir in the stock. Cook, stirring frequently to prevent scorching, until the fish is just warmed through, 3 to 4 minutes.

Add shrimp and crab meat. Cook, stirring occasionally, until shrimp is bright pink and plump, 5 to 6 minutes. Taste and add salt, if necessary. Divide among shallow bowls, top with remaining cilantro and serve immediately with lime wedges for squeezing.

author: Mark Bittman

ingredients.raw: 2 medium carrots, peeled and julienned or very thinly sliced
ingredients.preparation: peeled and julienned or very thinly sliced

ingredients.raw: 1 green apple, washed and julienned or very thinly sliced
ingredients.preparation: washed and julienned or very thinly sliced

ingredients.preparation: minced, or ½ tablespoon hot pepper flakes, or to taste

name: Ebon Moss-Bachrach’s Vegetarian Borscht
author: The New York Times
description: More savory than sweet, this Ukrainian cabbage and beet soup is one that the actor Ebon Moss-Bachrach learned from his beloved late mother-in-law, Lidia Yemchuk. The soup’s complex flavor stems in part from allowing the cabbage and onions to cook long enough that the water evaporates and the sugars caramelize. While Mr. Moss-Bachrach lets the soup rest overnight on the counter, refrigerating is recommended and will still allow the flavors of the dish to blend and deepen. Serve the soup hot or cold with a dollop of sour cream swirled in, for a vibrant magenta color, and a sprinkle of fragrant dill. If serving cold, diced fresh cucumber and chopped hard-boiled egg are particularly nice additions.

ingredients.raw: ½ medium to large head green cabbage
ingredients.item: medium to large head green cabbage

ingredients.raw: 4 medium to large red beets (about fist-sized)
ingredients.item: medium to large red beets (about fist-sized)

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large Dutch oven or soup pot over low.

Meanwhile, core and thinly slice the cabbage and dice the onions, adding them to the pot as you work, along with a big pinch of salt. Increase the heat to medium-high and cook, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables have softened, released their moisture, and begun to develop a little color, about 25 minutes. Don't rush this step: the cabbage should cook for quite a while, as this is where much of the soup's flavor develops.
While the cabbage is cooking, dice the carrots, mince the garlic and peel and dice the beets.
Once the cabbage is slightly caramelized, add the carrots, garlic and a pinch of salt to the pot and cook for another 2 to 3 minutes, until fragrant, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the diced beets and another big pinch of salt.Cook, stirring occasionally, for about 5 minutes.
Fill the pot with water until the vegetables are well covered. Bring to a boil on high, then reduce the heat to a gentle simmer. Simmer until the vegetables are tender, about 1 hour.
Remove the pot from the heat and stir in the juice of 1 lemon. Taste and add more salt or lemon juice, if desired.
Let the soup cool slightly then cover and let it rest, ideally overnight, in the refrigerator. The flavor improves significantly on the second and third day.
Serve hot or cold, topped with sour cream and dill. If serving cold, you can add diced cucumber or chopped hard-boiled egg, or both, as desired.

name: Ebony’s Rose Petal Pudding
author: Kayla Stewart
description: Freda DeKnight introduced many signature dishes to Ebony magazine in the mid-20th century. One was her rose petal pudding, which was beloved by Ebony staffers and readers alike. Although its origin story is unclear, it’s likely that Ms. DeKnight, the magazine’s food editor and a frequent traveler, created the dessert from her research and willingness to incorporate international flavors into her cooking. This warm pudding provides a sweet taste of one of the most significant culinary periods in the nation. The rose icing is divine, and the aromatic pudding, which resembles bread pudding, is really lovely. The original recipe calls for ¼ cup of rose water, which will give the pudding a very pronounced floral flavor, so you can choose an amount that is pleasing to you. Kayla Stewart

ingredients.raw: 10 tablespoons/143 grams unsalted butter, softened, plus more for the mold
ingredients.preparation: softened, plus more for the mold

ingredients.raw: 6 slices/242 grams white bread, toasted and finely ground (about 3 cups)
1 ½ cups/226 grams almonds, finely ground or 2 ¼ cups/226 grams almond flour
ingredients.preparation: finely ground or 2 ¼ cups/226 grams almond flour

ingredients.raw: ¼ packed cup/4 grams dried edible small rose petals, picked over for stems
ingredients.item: packed cup/4 grams dried edible small rose petals

ingredients.raw: 1 tablespoon rose water, plus more if desired
¼ cup/87 grams currant jelly or seedless raspberry jam
ingredients.item: /87 grams currant jelly or seedless raspberry jam

ingredients.raw: 2 tablespoons whole milk or cream, plus more as needed
Crystallized rose petals, for garnish (optional; see Tip)

steps.text: Make the pudding: Butter a 7- to 8-cup heatproof pudding mold or other deep baking dish or bowl.

Meanwhile, combine the bread crumbs, sugar, almonds, baking powder, salt, mace and rose petals in a large bowl or bowl of a stand mixer. Using an electric hand mixer or the paddle attachment of a stand mixer, mix the dry ingredients just to blend, about 10 seconds, then add the butter and beat until well combined, about 1 minute. In a medium bowl, beat the eggs with the milk, lemon juice and rose water. Add to the bread mixture and beat until everything is evenly moistened, about 1 minute.
Spoon the pudding mixture into the prepared mold; it should come two-thirds up the sides of the mold. Cover tightly with aluminum foil, crimping it around the edges to seal.

Place the covered mold in a wide pot or Dutch oven large enough to fit it with space around and over it. Add enough water to the pot to meet the middle of the bowl. Bring the water to a boil over medium heat, then cover the pot and reduce the heat to maintain a low simmer. Steam, replenishing with boiling water as needed so there’s always enough to reach the middle of the bowl, until a skewer inserted in the center comes out clean, 1 ½ to 2 hours. Cover tightly with foil again if the pudding needs to continue steaming after you insert the skewer.

When the pudding is done, uncover the pot and let the pudding cool in the pot for about 5 minutes. Wearing oven mitts or protecting your hands with kitchen towels, grip the mold and transfer it to a heatproof work surface. If the pudding seems stuck to the mold, run a thin knife or spatula around the edges of the mold. Center a serving plate larger than the mold over the mold, then hold both tightly together and flip. The pudding should release onto the plate. If it hasn’t, tap the mold a few times, then lift off the mold. Let the pudding cool to warm.

While the pudding cools slightly, make the icing: In a medium bowl, combine the confectioners’ sugar, butter, jelly, mace and rose water. Beat or whisk until smooth, then stir in the milk. If the icing is too thick to pour, add more milk by the tablespoon.
While the pudding is still warm, coat it with the icing. If you have any icing leftover, serve alongside the pudding. Decorate the pudding using the crystalized rose petals if you’d like. Serve warm.

name: Ebony’s Stewed Chicken and Dumplings
author: Kayla Stewart
description: This warming dish remains a constant in African American cuisine. Comforting and indulgent, it follows a formula that was familiar to Ebony’s audience. Published in 1962, the original recipe from the food editor Freda DeKnight called for a 4 ½- to 5-pound stewing hen which, she wrote, could take 2 to 3 ½ hours to cook “depending on the age and quality of the bird.” Today, smaller, fresh young chickens are readily available in most supermarkets, so the meat becomes tender much more quickly, making it easier to dig into this one-bowl meal even faster. Kayla Stewart

ingredients.raw: ½ cup chopped celery with tops
½ teaspoon flavor enhancer, such as Ac’cent or chicken bouillon granules
ingredients.preparation: such as Ac’cent or chicken bouillon granules

ingredients.raw: 2 tablespoons finely chopped parsley, plus more for garnish

steps.text: Prepare the chicken: Cut the chicken into 8 pieces with the back bones (2 breasts, 2 thighs, 2 drumsticks, 2 wings). You also can buy the chicken already cut up. Place in a large, heavy cooking pot or Dutch oven and add the onion, celery, salt, flavor enhancer, garlic salt, paprika and enough cold water to just cover the meat (about 4 cups).
Cover and bring to a boil over high heat. Skim any foam from the surface, then reduce the heat to low and simmer gently until the chicken is almost completely tender, about 45 minutes.
When the chicken is almost done, make the dumplings: Whisk the flour, baking powder, sugar and salt in a medium bowl. Add the milk and stir to form a thick, smooth batter.

Uncover the pot and drop heaping teaspoons of the dumpling batter on top of the chicken, spacing apart slightly. Sprinkle with the parsley and cover the pot. Cook for 20 minutes without lifting the lid. If you cut into a dumpling, the dough should be cooked through to the center. Serve the chicken and dumplings on a platter or in serving dishes, garnished with more parsley.
